name: Russia-Ukraine long-range strike war
summary: Both sides wage a nightly long-range war. Russia fires hundreds of drones, increasingly jet-powered, plus ballistic and cruise missiles at Ukraine's power grid, cities and ports, while Ukraine hits Russian refineries, arms plants, airbases and ships up to 2,300 km away. Civilian casualties in Ukraine hit a multi-year high in September 2026.

sides.name: Russia (strikes on Ukraine)
members: Aerospace Forces and Long-Range Aviation (Kh-101, Kinzhal, Kh-59/69)
leaders: Valery Gerasimov (Chief of the General Staff)
sides.strength: In October 2025 Russia launched 9,298 drones and 270 missiles in a month (ISW). In August 2026 about 2,800 jet-powered drones (United24 headline). Typical October 2026 nights: 140 to 460 drones.

sides.name: Ukraine (air defence and strikes on Russia)
members: Ukrainian Air Force and air defence
Fire Point (FP-5 Flamingo cruise missile maker)
backers: Germany and US (Patriot systems and interceptors)
sides.strength: FP-5 Flamingo production about 100 per month (July 2026). In March 2026 Ukraine launched more one-way attack drones (7,500) than Russia launched at Ukraine (6,500).

background: Russia has struck Ukrainian cities and energy infrastructure since 2022, aiming to break morale, cripple industry and force concessions. Ukraine, short of Western long-range missiles and barred at times from using them inside Russia, built its own drone and missile industry and turned it on Russia's oil refining, defence factories and Black Sea Fleet. The strike war matters because it sets the economic cost of the war for both countries, decides whether Ukrainians have heat and power in winter, and is reshaping air defence everywhere: cheap drones are now exhausting missiles that cost millions.
year: Russia renewed mass energy strikes in autumn 2025, launching 9,298 drones and 270 missiles in October 2025 alone, with Ukrenergo counting eight massive combined strikes between October and December. By late January DTEK said Ukraine's generation capacity had fallen 60 to 70%, and a single raid on 23 to 24 January left more than 800,000 Kyiv subscribers without power. On 8 January 2026 Russia fired an Oreshnik intermediate-range missile at the Lviv aviation repair plant, the first ballistic strike on Lviv Oblast, and in January Zelensky declared an energy emergency. Putin agreed to Trump's request to pause strikes on Kyiv until 1 February, but the pause was not extended. The largest missile attack of 2026 came on 23 to 24 May: 90 missiles (36 ballistic, including an Oreshnik) and 600 drones, centred on Kyiv. Ukraine downed 91.5% of drones but only 36.7% of Iskander-type ballistic missiles, exposing its Patriot shortage. Over the summer Russia shifted to jet-powered Shahed variants (Geran-3 and Shahed-238) that are harder to catch; Ukraine stopped publishing missile counts on 11 August, and September brought renewed systematic grid strikes and the worst civilian toll in years. Ukraine in turn went deeper: FP-5 Flamingo cruise missiles hit plants at Votkinsk, Chapaevsk, Cheboksary, Volgograd, Kirov and Samara; a Sub Sea Baby underwater drone struck a Kilo-class submarine at Novorossiysk on 15 December 2025; drones destroyed two Tu-142s near Taganrog in May 2026; the July 'Crimean Switch Off' hit 104 substations; Azov Sea strikes hit about 116 ships; and in October Ukraine destroyed four Su-34s at Borisoglebsk, hit a gas condensate plant near Surgut 2,340 km away and struck microchip, titanium and data-centre targets. At sea, both sides attack shipping: more than 570 vessels were affected in 2026 and Russia has carried out about 90% of strikes on civilian ships since 10 September, nearly shutting Odesa's ports.
situation: As of 12 November 2026 both sides are striking each other's energy systems nightly, and the Abu Dhabi talks on 10 and 11 November produced no energy or Black Sea truce. Russia typically launches 150 to 450 drones a night, about half of them jet-powered, plus ballistic and cruise missiles in larger waves, aimed at the substations that move power between regions and link the nuclear plants to the grid, and at rail, ports and gas facilities. Overnight into 11 November it hit six large substations in Vinnytsia, Kirovohrad, Zhytomyr and Cherkasy regions and rail lines in Dnipropetrovsk and Zhytomyr regions (Prime Minister Serhiy Koretsky), leaving parts of eight regions without power, including about 135,000 consumers in Odesa region. Earlier waves blacked out more than 600,000 people in Dnipropetrovsk region on 8 November, cut Kyiv's power and heating on 7 November, and left the occupied Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant on diesel for the 16th time this year. Guided bombs remain the deadliest weapon near the front: the 2 November strikes on an aid point in Komyshuvakha killed at least 43. Ukraine hits Russian refineries, ports and defence plants with long-range drones and Neptune missiles: Kirishi, Saratov, Ryazan and Afipsky refineries burned between 5 and 9 November, and overnight into 11 November Russia said it downed 627 drones over 22 regions, the Sea of Azov and Crimea, as drones set the Baltic oil and grain port of Ust-Luga on fire and wounded three workers, debris killed two people in an apartment block in Yartsevo, Smolensk region, and Pulkovo airport in St Petersburg closed. Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania issued drone alerts and Finland briefly restricted airspace in the eastern Gulf of Finland. Ukraine's interception rate against jet drones is about 75%, and a 500-missile Patriot sale approved by the US on 30 October could take years to deliver. The shipping war has spread to the western Black Sea, where sea drones sank the Contship Jet off Bulgaria on 29 October, and Russia says it has hit cargo ships off Odesa. Overnight into 12 November Russia launched 123 drones, 73 of them jet-powered, with Iskander-M and Zircon missiles; regional officials counted 10 killed and 40 injured over the day, including at least four at a market in Chornomorsk and one in Kyiv, and Zelensky said disruption to the Starshield satellite network was weakening interception of jet drones (Reuters, AP, Ukrainska Pravda, Meduza, Kyiv Independent).
technical: Grid damage: DTEK estimated Ukraine's power generation capacity was down 60 to 70% by January 2026, with repair costs of 64 to 70 billion dollars; ISW said Ukraine urgently needed more PAC-3 Patriot interceptors.
Volume: Russia launched 9,298 drones and 270 missiles in October 2025, 5,444 drones and 216 missiles in November 2025, and 2,757 drones and 91 missiles in 1 to 15 December 2025 (ISW).

September 2026 Ukrainian Air Force tally: 2,722 Shahed-131/136 and 1,935 jet-powered Shahed-238 destroyed, plus 1,009 reconnaissance drones, 719 Lancets and 86 S8000 Banderol munitions; missiles destroyed included 24 Kh-101, 12 Kalibr, 8 Iskander-M/KN-23, 8 Zircon, 6 Iskander-K and 6 Kh-59/69.

Jet Shaheds: by October 2026 roughly half of each Russian drone raid is jet-powered (for example 108 of 149 on 15 to 16 October; 70 of 140 on 25 to 26 October). Zelensky cited a 57% interception rate for jet drones in September; ISW put it at 77% before a dip to about 74% in mid-October.
Geran-5: a jet drone with a 90 kg warhead and 1,000 km range that can be launched from Su-25 aircraft, per Ukrainian intelligence (January 2026).
Interceptor drones: in the 24 May 2026 attack Ukrainian interceptor drones accounted for more than 40% of downed Shaheds; Kyiv also fields 12+ automated Sky Sentinel anti-drone turrets.
Ballistic gap: on 24 May 2026 Ukraine stopped only 36.7% of Iskander-M/S-300 ballistic missiles versus 81.5% of cruise missiles; Patriot interceptor stocks were reported dwindling in September 2026.

Oreshnik: used on Lviv (8 January 2026) and twice on 24 May 2026 (one hit garages in Bila Tserkva near Kyiv, one fell in Russian-held Donetsk); footage showed six clusters of six kinetic rods; the system was declared on combat duty in Belarus on 30 December 2025.
Cruise missiles: Ukraine said it downed 88% of Kh-101, Kh-55 and Kh-555 missiles launched from January to early May 2026.
Reporting blackout: Ukraine stopped regularly publishing missile launch and intercept figures on 11 August 2026, making Russian missile use harder to track.

FP-5 Flamingo: claimed 3,000 km range, about 1,150 kg warhead (possibly 925 kg) and 850 to 950 km/h; production rose from about 30 a month in August 2025 to about 100 a month by July 2026. Russia's A-50U helped shoot down a five-missile salvo aimed at Votkinsk on 4 July 2026.
Ukrainian deep-strike reach: Ukhta refinery in Komi (about 1,750 km, February 2026) and Gazprom's condensate plant near Surgut in Khanty-Mansi (about 2,340 km, October 2026).

Target shift: in 2026 Ukraine moved beyond oil to defence electronics (Energiya Yelets, Proton-Electrotex Oryol), titanium (VSMPO-AVISMA Berezniki), explosives (Chapaevsk), missile plants (Votkinsk) and Yandex data centres; Storm Shadow reportedly hit Yelets on 24 to 25 October 2026.
Ukrainian drone forces claim at least 225 strikes on Russian energy targets by December 2025, cutting Russian oil processing capacity by about 20%.

Naval drones: Sub Sea Baby UUVs hit a Project 636 Kilo-class submarine carrying Kalibr launchers at Novorossiysk on 15 December 2025, which ISW calls the first underwater-drone strike on a submarine; maritime drones also damaged tankers near the CPC terminal in January 2026.

Shipping war: Ambrey and the IMO count more than 570 vessels hit in the Black Sea in 2026, 387 in July to September, with at least 40 sailors killed; fewer than 10 ships used Greater Odesa ports in September 2026 against about 400 in July.
casualties: UN HRMMU: civilian casualties from long-range missiles and drones rose 60% in January to June 2026 compared with 2025, and 328 civilians were killed and 2,105 injured in September 2026, 85% more than in September 2025, with Kyiv hit on 22 of 30 days; the UN called early October among the deadliest periods in years. Russian authorities reported 250 civilians killed and 1,596 injured on Russian territory in January to June 2026 (unverified). The 24 May 2026 strike killed at least 4 and injured over 100. In Russia, CIT counted 472 civilians killed in western Russia from 2025 to 31 July 2026. Figures are verified minimums.
displaced: Strikes drive temporary displacement from frontline and border cities such as Kharkiv, Sumy, Kherson and Zaporizhzhia; no 2026 strike-specific displacement figure found.

timeline.event: October 2025 total: 9,298 Russian drones and 270 missiles launched at Ukraine.
Ukrainian Sub Sea Baby underwater drones hit a Kilo-class submarine at Novorossiysk.
Russia says Oreshnik missiles in Belarus are on combat duty.
Oreshnik strikes the Lviv State Aviation Repair Plant.
FP-5 Flamingo missiles hit the Votkinsk plant, which builds Iskander missiles, about 1,400 km away.
Largest missile strike of 2026: 90 missiles including Oreshnik and 600 drones, centred on Kyiv.
Ukrainian drones destroy two Tu-142 aircraft and an Iskander launcher near Taganrog.
Ukraine says 104 Crimean substations and power sites were hit since 1 July ('Crimean Switch Off').
Ukraine stops regularly publishing missile launch and intercept numbers.
Putin orders a 72-hour pause on strikes on Kyiv during the US envoys' visit.
Major Russian attack damages generation, distribution and transmission in three regions and Kyiv; September civilian casualties hit a multi-year high.
Satellite imagery confirms four Su-34s destroyed at Borisoglebsk; first Ukrainian strike in Khanty-Mansi, near Surgut.
Storm Shadow reportedly hits the Energiya plant at Yelets; strikes on Berezniki titanium plant and Oryol microchip plant.
16 ballistic missiles and about 280 drones target Kyiv; the Southern Bridge is hit and closed and a double-tap strike hits rescuers at a university campus.
A Russian jet-powered drone hits a crowded train platform in Dnipro, killing at least 13 people (Zelensky); the toll later rose to 15 (Kyiv Independent).

Drones sink the Greek-operated container ship Contship Jet in Bulgaria's exclusive economic zone; the crew is rescued. Attribution is unconfirmed, but Ambrey assesses the drone as derived from the Russian Murena-300S design, and at least six ships have been hit off Bulgaria this month.

Russia hits Dnipro station again a day later; Russian Deputy PM Novak says three refineries and a gas-chemical plant were attacked, including Novokuybyshevsk, despite WSJ reports that Ukraine had paused refinery strikes under US pressure.
US State Department approves a 2.1 billion dollar sale of 500 Patriot missiles to Ukraine; Zelensky warns delivery could take years.
Russia launches 433 drones overnight at energy sites, leaving hundreds of thousands without power; drones hit an industrial site in Kstovo, Nizhny Novgorod region, reported to be Lukoil's refinery.
Ukraine's air raid app sends fake nuclear and chemical alerts after what the air force calls enemy interference; Russia says its own alert app was hit by a cyberattack early on 2 November.
Russia launches 193 drones overnight; guided bombs on Izium kill one, injure 11 and cut the city's power.
Guided bombs hit an aid distribution point at a school in Komyshuvakha, Zaporizhzhia region, then a shelter; at least 29 killed and 48 missing by 3 November.

Russia fires 289 drones, 17 ballistic and 59 cruise missiles at nine regions overnight; at least 62 wounded in Kharkiv, one killed in Dnipro. Russia says it downed 856 Ukrainian drones, 493 aimed at Moscow; Yaroslavl refinery hit.

Russia sends 310 drones overnight, 272 downed, hitting energy sites in Zhytomyr, Kovel, Ternopil and Rivne and a shopping centre in Odesa; Ukrainian drones set an Ozon logistics centre in Adygea on fire and Russia claims 709 drones downed.

Police say 42 bodies have been recovered at Komyshuvakha, with up to 33 more feared trapped. More than 200 Ukrainian drones attack Ryazan region and the Ryazan refinery burns; Russia sends 128 drones, 105 downed.
Zelensky says the Komyshuvakha toll has risen to 43; Russian-installed officials say a Ukrainian strike on a bus in occupied Luhansk region kills five.
Russia sends 227 drones overnight, 196 downed or jammed; a Ukrainian drone attack reportedly sets the Afipsky refinery in Krasnodar region on fire.

Russia fires 36 ballistic missiles and 172 drones at energy sites around Kyiv and the Northern Bridge, injuring five in Kyiv; Ukrainian drones set the Saratov refinery on fire and Neptune missiles hit a plant in Oryol (RFE/RL, AP). AP puts the Komyshuvakha toll at 55.

Strikes black out more than 600,000 people in Dnipropetrovsk region and about 250,000 customers in Kharkiv region (AFP); the Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant loses its last grid line and runs on diesel for the 16th time this year (Energoatom).

Russia launches 317 drones and Banderol cruise missiles overnight; a jet drone kills three at an Odesa infrastructure site; Ukrainian drones set the Kirishi refinery on fire, killing one woman (Ukrinform, RFE/RL). Russia says it hit three cargo ships off Odesa and Chornomorsk on 8 November (Reuters, unverified).

Russia launches 162 drones and a ballistic missile overnight as Abu Dhabi talks open; Russia says it downed 155 Ukrainian drones, and occupied Luhansk loses power after a Ukrainian drone attack (AP, TASS).

Russia hits six large substations in four central regions and rail in two, cutting power in parts of eight regions; Ukrainian drones set Ust-Luga port on fire and Russia claims 627 drones downed; two killed in Yartsevo, Smolensk region; Baltic states issue drone alerts (Reuters, RFE/RL, Meduza).

Russia launches 123 drones and Iskander-M and Zircon missiles as US envoys fly to Moscow; officials report 10 killed and 40 injured over the day, including at least four at a market in Chornomorsk and one in Kyiv (Kyiv Independent, ABC News).

outlook: Watch whether Russia repeats last winter's grid campaign at higher volume with jet drones, and whether Ukraine can field cheap jet-capable interceptors and get more Patriot missiles. The 10 to 11 November Abu Dhabi talks produced no energy or Black Sea moratorium, so watch for one in any follow-up round, Russian attempts to close Odesa's ports entirely, and Ukrainian strikes on Russia's defence electronics and data infrastructure. Drone incursions into Moldova and suspected Russian sabotage in Europe show the strike war's spillover risk.

zones.note: Main target of Russia's largest 2026 combined strikes, including Oreshnik on 24 May; civilian casualties on 22 of 30 days in September 2026.

zones.name: Kharkiv
zones.note: Daily drone and glide-bomb strikes, including double-tap strikes on rescuers; 280,000 customers lost power on 16 October 2026.

zones.name: Odesa ports
zones.note: Russian strikes on ports and ships cut traffic from about 400 ships in July to fewer than 10 in September 2026.

zones.name: Lviv and western Ukraine
zones.note: Oreshnik strike on the Lviv aviation repair plant on 8 January 2026; Volyn grid strikes in October.

zones.name: Novorossiysk naval base
zones.note: Black Sea Fleet base hit by Ukrainian underwater drones in December 2025.

zones.name: Crimea
zones.note: Ukrainian strikes on air defence, fuel trains and power; 104 substations hit in July 2026.

zones.name: Sea of Azov
zones.note: Ukrainian air and sea drones struck about 116 ships in July to August 2026; Volga-Don canal shipping halted.

zones.name: Russian border belt: Belgorod, Kursk, Bryansk, Voronezh, Oryol, Lipetsk
zones.note: Ukrainian strikes on radars, airbases (Borisoglebsk), power plants and defence-electronics factories.

zones.name: Volga industrial belt
zones.note: Flamingo and drone strikes on refineries and arms plants at Volgograd, Samara, Chapaevsk, Cheboksary, Kirov and Votkinsk.

battles.name: Russian guided-bomb strike on a Komyshuvakha aid distribution point
battles.place: Komyshuvakha, Zaporizhzhia Raion, Zaporizhzhia Oblast, Ukraine
sides: Russia: guided aerial bombs (KABs)
Ukraine: civilians collecting humanitarian aid at a school, then police and rescuers at a nearby shelter
battles.outcome: Bombs hit a school used weekly as an aid distribution point, and about nine more hit a shelter where police and rescuers had taken cover after a new strike warning, according to Zelensky.
battles.forces: Guided aerial bombs dropped by Russian aircraft (Kyiv Independent, AP).
battles.losses: At least 55 killed (AP, 7 November), up from 50 given by Ukraine's State Emergency Service on 6 November (Al Jazeera), with dozens still missing; earlier counts were 42, including four police officers and two rescue workers (national police, 5 November), and the toll was 24 on 2 November and 29 on 3 November (acting regional governor Mykhailo Semikin), with at least five injured.
battles.significance: One of the deadliest single attacks on Ukrainian civilians in 2026, in a village about 20 km from the front, the morning after the Oleshky truce ended.

battles.name: Russian drone strike on a Dnipro train platform
sides: Russia: jet-powered attack drone
Ukraine: civilians boarding train No. 866 to Zaporizhzhia
battles.outcome: A jet-powered drone hit an open platform as passengers boarded; sirens sounded but the drone arrived too fast for staff to clear the platform.
battles.forces: One jet-powered attack drone (Ukrainian rail operator and Scripps News).
battles.losses: At least 15 civilians killed and 14 wounded (Kyiv Independent, 30 October); Zelensky first gave 13 dead and Reuters later at least 14.
battles.significance: One of the deadliest single strikes on Ukrainian civilians in autumn 2026, and part of a Russian campaign against rail hubs, coming during the localised Oleshky ceasefire.

battles.name: Ukrainian strikes on Russian defence-electronics plants (Yelets, Oryol, Berezniki, Voronezh)
sides: Ukraine: Storm Shadow missiles and drones
Russia: Energiya plant, Proton-Electrotex, VSMPO-AVISMA, Voronezh aircraft plant
battles.outcome: Energiya plant at Yelets (Iskander power cells) reportedly hit by Storm Shadow; Proton-Electrotex microchip workshops in Oryol damaged; VSMPO-AVISMA titanium plant in Berezniki (about 1,580 km) struck; Voronezh aircraft and synthetic-rubber plants hit.
battles.forces: Storm Shadow cruise missiles and long-range drones.
battles.significance: Shows Ukraine targeting the electronics and materials Russia needs for missiles and aircraft, not just oil.

battles.name: Strike on Borisoglebsk airbase
battles.place: Borisoglebsk airbase (6 km east of Borisoglebsk; coordinates approximate), Voronezh Oblast, Russia
sides: Ukraine: long-range strike forces
Russia: Aerospace Forces Su-34 regiment
battles.outcome: Satellite imagery confirms four Su-34 bombers destroyed; Ukraine also claimed two damaged. Date shown is when ISW reported the satellite confirmation.
battles.losses: Four Su-34 destroyed, two damaged (Ukrainian claim for the damaged).
battles.significance: Su-34s are Russia's main glide-bomb carriers, so each one lost reduces KAB attacks on front-line towns.

sources.label: ISW/Critical Threats: Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment, October 16, 2026

battles.name: Drone strike on Gazprom's Surgut condensate plant
battles.place: Near Surgut, Khanty-Mansi Autonomous Okrug, Russia
sides: Ukraine: long-range drones
Russia: Gazprom Chernomyrdin Condensate Stabilization Plant
battles.outcome: Fire started at the plant, the first reported Ukrainian strike in the region.
battles.significance: At about 2,340 km from Ukraine it is among the deepest strikes of the war, showing no part of Russia's energy system west of Siberia is safe.

sources.label: ISW/Critical Threats: Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment, October 16, 2026

battles.name: Russian strikes on Odesa ports and Black Sea shipping
battles.place: Greater Odesa ports, Odesa Oblast, Ukraine
sides: Russia: drone and missile forces
Ukraine: port operators, Navy and air defence
battles.outcome: Ongoing. Russia accounts for about 90% of strikes on civilian shipping since 10 September; fewer than 10 ships passed Greater Odesa ports in September 2026 against about 400 in July.
battles.forces: Drones and missiles against ports and vessels.
battles.losses: More than 570 vessels affected by strikes in the Black Sea in 2026, 387 in July to September, at least 40 sailors killed (Ambrey and IMO via the Financial Times).
battles.significance: Threatens Ukraine's export economy and global grain supply; it is why Zelensky offers a Black Sea strike moratorium.

sides: Ukraine: Unmanned Systems Forces

battles.outcome: Ukraine says 104 substations and power facilities were hit in 20 days.
battles.significance: Turned Russia's grid-war logic back on occupied Crimea, which supplies Russian forces in the south.

sides: Ukraine: air and sea drones
Russia: merchant and tanker fleet, Black Sea Fleet
battles.outcome: About 116 ships reportedly struck, at least 57 of them tankers; Russia halted Volga-Don canal shipping on 10 July 2026.
battles.losses: Not reported in sources used here.
battles.significance: Cut a key Russian logistics route from the Volga to the occupied south and Crimea.

battles.name: Drone strike on Taganrog airfield
sides: Ukraine: Unmanned Systems Forces
Russia: Naval aviation and missile troops
battles.outcome: Two Tu-142 maritime patrol aircraft and an Iskander launcher destroyed, per Ukrainian sources.
battles.losses: Two Tu-142 and one Iskander launcher (Ukrainian claim).
battles.significance: Rare, hard-to-replace naval aviation airframes destroyed close to the front, part of a 2026 Ukrainian focus on Russian aircraft and missile launchers.

battles.name: 23-24 May 2026 combined strike on Kyiv
battles.place: Kyiv and Bila Tserkva, Kyiv Oblast, Ukraine
sides: Russia: Aerospace Forces, missile brigades, Navy, drone units
Ukraine: Air Force, Patriot and other air defence, interceptor drones
battles.outcome: Largest missile strike of 2026. Ukraine downed 55 of 90 missiles and 549 of 600 drones; 16 missiles and 51 drones hit 54 locations.
battles.forces: 90 missiles (1 Oreshnik, 2 Kinzhal, 3 Zircon, 30 Iskander-M or S-300, 54 Kh-101, Iskander-K or Kalibr) plus 600 drones including jet Geran-3 and Geran-4. A second Oreshnik landed in Russian-held Donetsk.
battles.losses: At least 4 killed and over 100 injured; Foreign Ministry, Cabinet of Ministers building and National Art Museum damaged; Chornobyl Museum and Lukianivskyi market destroyed.
battles.significance: Showed Ukraine's ballistic-defence gap (only 36.7% of Iskander-type missiles stopped) and the first Oreshnik use against the Kyiv region; Ukrainian interceptor drones got over 40% of Shahed kills.

battles.name: FP-5 Flamingo strike on the Votkinsk plant
sides: Ukraine: Flamingo cruise missiles (Fire Point)

battles.outcome: Plant hit about 1,400 km from Ukraine; 11 people injured according to reports. A later five-missile salvo at Votkinsk on 4 July 2026 was reportedly shot down with help from an A-50U.
battles.significance: Votkinsk makes Iskander ballistic missiles, so the strike went after the weapons Ukraine struggles to intercept, using a home-built missile.

battles.name: 23-24 January 2026 strike on Kyiv's power system
sides: Russia: missile and drone forces
Ukraine: Air Force and air defence
battles.outcome: Ukraine intercepted 15 of 21 missiles and 357 of 375 drones, but hits on energy facilities left more than 800,000 Kyiv subscribers and 400,000 in Chernihiv without power, with hourly outages across most of Ukraine.
battles.forces: 6 Iskander-M or S-300, 2 Zircon, 12 Kh-22/32 and 1 Kh-59/69 missiles plus 375 drones (about 250 Shahed-type).
battles.losses: One civilian killed in Kyiv and dozens wounded; at least 31 injured in Kharkiv.
battles.significance: Struck while US, Ukrainian and Russian delegations were meeting in Abu Dhabi, at the low point of last winter's grid crisis when DTEK put generation capacity down 60 to 70%.

battles.name: Oreshnik strike on Lviv
battles.place: Lviv State Aviation Repair Plant, Lviv, Ukraine
sides: Russia: Strategic Missile Forces (Oreshnik launched from Kapustin Yar)
Ukraine: Air Force air defence
battles.outcome: Strike delivered as part of a wider drone and missile attack; first ballistic missile strike on Lviv Oblast.
battles.forces: One Oreshnik intermediate-range ballistic missile with multiple kinetic or inert submunitions, launched from Kapustin Yar.
battles.losses: Damage not described in sources used here.
battles.significance: Second combat use of Oreshnik and a signal to Europe, coming days after Russia declared Oreshnik units in Belarus on combat duty.

battles.name: Sub Sea Baby strike on a Kilo-class submarine at Novorossiysk
battles.place: Novorossiysk Naval Base, Krasnodar Krai, Russia
sides: Ukraine: SBU with Sub Sea Baby unmanned underwater vehicles
Russia: Black Sea Fleet
battles.outcome: Ukrainian strike hit a Project 636 Varshavyanka submarine; fires seen near the base on satellite heat data.
battles.forces: Unmanned underwater vehicles; the target carried four Kalibr launch tubes according to the SBU.
battles.losses: Extent of damage not independently confirmed.
battles.significance: ISW calls it the first underwater-drone strike on a submarine in naval history; it pushes the Black Sea Fleet's Kalibr carriers further from safety even in their main base.

battles.name: Russian strike campaign on Ukraine's energy grid (2025-2026)
battles.place: Nationwide, centred on Kyiv, Kharkiv, Odesa and Dnipropetrovsk, Ukraine
sides: Russia: drone and missile forces
Ukraine: Air Force, Ukrenergo, DTEK and repair crews
battles.outcome: Ongoing. Eight massive combined strikes on energy between October and December 2025; Ukraine declared an energy emergency in January 2026; systematic grid strikes resumed in September 2026.
battles.forces: 9,298 drones and 270 missiles in October 2025; 5,444 drones and 216 missiles in November 2025. In October 2026 raids of 140 to 460 drones a night, about half jet-powered.
battles.losses: Civilian casualties in September 2026 were 85% higher than a year earlier; hundreds of thousands of customers lose power after major raids (270,000 in Volyn and 280,000 in Kharkiv on 16 October 2026).
battles.significance: Russia's main lever for pressuring Ukrainian society and the reason Ukraine offers an energy-strike moratorium in talks.
